feature: Microsoft Changes (#1485, screen 03; Feature #1494) — the real Microsoft Changes page in artifacts/portal, wired to the already-built GET /api/portal/message-center (docs/portal/microsoft-changes-contract-pack.md §1a) and the decline write POST /api/portal/change-control/:code/decline (§1c). Real design landed in Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/screens/Microsoft Changes.dc.html; page lives at artifacts/portal/src/pages/microsoft-changes.tsx, route /microsoft-changes. This build also added the `routing` field to the message-center wire (joining m365_change_routings + msp_change_requests) — the customer wire had no field connecting a post to its routed Change Request at all before this.
notes: shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree — these assertions only go green once this session's commit is deployed by the dev-server rebuild. NOT RUN THIS SESSION: the dev-server checkout is blocked on #3054 (93+ commits behind origin/main, merge-back coordinator fails on a spurious add/add conflict) — confirmed still open at the time of this build, same failure #2992's bookend already documented. Verified instead by: tsc --noEmit clean on both artifacts/api-server and artifacts/portal, and the new routing join hand-checked against real rows in the local DATABASE_URL (m365_change_routings id=3/4, msp_change_requests currently empty locally so the dangling change_request_id=83 case was exercised directly — the join deliberately keys `changeRequestCode` off the JOINED msp_change_requests.id, not the routing row's own soft FK, so a dangling reference yields no code rather than a code for a CR that doesn't exist).

apiTests prove the real, already-built backend contract directly: log in via POST /api/auth/login, extract a bearer token, then GET /api/portal/message-center exactly as microsoft-changes.tsx's own fetchWithAuth call does.

TEST1 covers the honest-empty case that is ALSO the live case in local dev right now: analysedCount can legitimately be 0 or low (contract pack's own 'dormant pipeline' caveat) — the assertions below check SHAPE (keys exist, buckets has the fixed 11-entry axis, dateUnclearPosts/posts are arrays), not a specific count, so the manifest does not need re-pinning as real interpretations/routings are authored over time.

TEST4/TEST5 assert the NEW `routing` field this build added exists as a key on a post (present-but-null is a valid, honest state) — this is the regression guard for the gap this build closed (the wire previously had no field connecting a post to its Change Request at all).

UI STEPS drive the real page: login through the real Auth Core login page (#2991, Feature #1648), then assert the page's own dataState machine (loading → live), the 4 real stat cards, the triage section (empty-state asserted, since the local testbed tenant currently has zero actionable 'approval'-intake routings — MC1287370's real routing is intake=informed, which the page correctly excludes from triage), and the horizon wave-0 selection driving the 'In this wave' panel.

ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD — the same Customer testbed account test-manifests/portal/customer-home-landing.json and test-manifests/portal/notification-preferences.json already use.

NO WRITE IS EXERCISED by this manifest. The decline action (surface C) needs a real actionable routing (decision=auto_created, intake=approval, an existing msp_change_requests row) to test end-to-end, which does not exist in local dev at the time of writing (see TEST1 note) — wiring is covered by the route's own existing tests in artifacts/api-server (portal-change-control.ts) and by direct code review of the decline() call in useMicrosoftChangesLive.ts. Exercising it here once real routed data exists is a natural follow-up, not a gap being silently skipped.
